### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.
- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.

### Reproducible Example

In a fresh virtualenv with **only** `pandas==3.0.4` (and its required deps `numpy`, `python-dateutil`) installed on **CPython 3.14**:

```python
import pandas as pd

pd.Timedelta(days=28)   # Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault
```

Any `Timedelta` constructor crashes the interpreter at construction time — `pd.Timedelta(days=28)`, `pd.Timedelta("28 days")`, `pd.Timedelta(28, "D")`. No DataFrame/Series is involved, no threading, single-threaded `python -c`.

### Issue Description

Constructing a `pandas.Timedelta` segfaults immediately on **pandas 3.0.4 / CPython 3.14**. This is a **regression from 3.0.3** — in the same virtualenv, downgrading only `pandas` (`3.0.4` → `3.0.3`, numpy unchanged) makes the example work, and upgrading back to `3.0.4` crashes again. So `pandas` is the only changed variable.

It reproduces with numpy **2.3.3** (pandas 3.0.4's own declared minimum for Python 3.14, `numpy>=2.3.3`) and with numpy **2.4.6**, so it is not specific to a single numpy build.

With `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1`, the C stack shows what looks like unbounded recursion between `pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas` and numpy's `_multiarray_umath`, overflowing the C stack:

```
Current thread's C stack trace (most recent call first):
  ...python... _Py_DumpStack
  /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x45330)
  numpy/_core/_multiarray_umath.cpython-314-x86_64-linux-gnu.so(+0x101f18)
  pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.cpython-314-x86_64-linux-gnu.so(+0x541ac)
  pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.cpython-314-x86_64-linux-gnu.so(+0x590ac)
  python _PyObject_MakeTpCall+0x1e7
  pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.cpython-314-x86_64-linux-gnu.so(+0x51f12)   # (deeper frames repeat the
  pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.cpython-314-x86_64-linux-gnu.so(+0x590ac)   #  timedeltas +0x590ac <-> MakeTpCall pattern)
  python _PyObject_MakeTpCall+0x1e7
  ...
```

The Python-level stack is just the single `pd.Timedelta(...)` call line — the fault is entirely in the compiled extension.

I haven't bisected which 3.0.4 commit introduced it, but the only `_libs` source change between 3.0.3 and 3.0.4 that touches this area is the datetime C code (e.g. the `np_datetime.c` include-order change, #65591/#65609); the maintainers will know best where to look.

### Expected Behavior

`pd.Timedelta(days=28)` returns `Timedelta('28 days 00:00:00')`, as it does on pandas 3.0.3.

Note: this currently makes pandas 3.0.4 unusable for any downstream library that constructs a `Timedelta` at import time (e.g. importing RAPIDS cuDF segfaults for this reason).

I have only been able to test CPython **3.14.6** so far (couldn't easily build other interpreters in this environment); I don't yet know whether 3.11–3.13 are affected.

Adversarial testing of the parallel `read_csv` path added in GH-64347 turned up several cases where the parallel result diverges from the serial (`mode.max_threads=1`) result on the *same* file. Reporting them together since most share a root cause. All reproduce on `main` through the default path on a non-Windows machine (files must exceed the 50 MB parallel threshold).

### Root cause for most of these: the parallel path ignores `low_memory=False`

`_can_parallelize_csv` never consults `low_memory`, so `read_csv(big_file, low_memory=False)` is still split into `n_workers` byte-range chunks. That reintroduces exactly the per-chunk type/NA-inference divergences that `low_memory=False` exists to prevent: a "lean" chunk sees a different value distribution than the whole file and infers differently. Bug 2 and Bug 3 below are both instances of this.

---

### 🔴 Bug 1 — `EmptyDataError` on a valid headerless file with a blank first line

`header=None` (without `names`) on a file whose first physical line is blank or whitespace-only raises, where the serial path reads it fine (it skips the blank line).

```python
import os, pandas as pd

with open("f1.csv", "wb") as fh:
    fh.write(b"\n")  # leading blank line
    fh.write(b"".join(f"{i},{i*2},x{i}\n".encode() for i in range(2_600_000)))  # ~59 MB

pd.read_csv("f1.csv", header=None)
# -> EmptyDataError: No columns to parse from file

with pd.option_context("mode.max_threads", 1):
    pd.read_csv("f1.csv", header=None)   # OK, (2600000, 3)
```

**Cause:** in `_read_csv_parallel`, column-name inference builds `name_buf = preamble + first_line`; when `first_line` is blank, `TextFileReader(name_buf, ...)` raises `EmptyDataError`. That is not a `ParserError` subclass, so the `except (ParserError, UnicodeDecodeError)` fallback in `_read` doesn't catch it. Also fires when `skiprows` lands `data_start` on a blank line with `header=None`. (The `names=[...]` form falls back cleanly via the `n_first_rows != 1` guard — only bare `header=None` crashes.)

**Fix:** catch `EmptyDataError` around the name-inference `TextFileReader` and `return None` (fall back). Falling back is always safe: if the serial path would also raise, we reproduce it. Validated locally, 78 tests in `test_parallel_read.py` still pass.

---

### 🔴 Bug 2 — `dtype_backend="pyarrow"` raises on large ints where serial succeeds

A chunk that sees only large integers (> 2⁵³) attempts a numeric/pyarrow conversion and raises, while the whole-file serial read keeps the column as `double`/string.

```python
import pandas as pd

BIG = "9223372036854775807"
with open("f2.csv", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("c0\n")
    fh.write("\n".join("1.5" if i == 2_000_000 else BIG for i in range(4_000_000)))  # ~76 MB
    fh.write("\n")

pd.read_csv("f2.csv", dtype_backend="pyarrow", low_memory=False)
# -> pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid: Integer value 9223372036854775807 not in range ...

with pd.option_context("mode.max_threads", 1):
    pd.read_csv("f2.csv", dtype_backend="pyarrow", low_memory=False)   # OK, dtype double[pyarrow]
```

The guard treats `int`-kind + `float`-kind chunks as safe to `concat`, which holds for numpy/`numpy_nullable` but not pyarrow (its `concat` does a checked int→double cast that fails above 2⁵³). Depending on magnitude the parallel path raises `ArrowInvalid` (int in `[2⁵³, 2⁶⁴)`) or `OverflowError` (`> 2⁶⁴`). This is **pyarrow-specific** — `numpy` and `numpy_nullable` match serial in all cases tested. Note that with the default `low_memory=True`, a large file makes the serial path chunk internally too, so *both* raise; the clean parallel-only regression is under `low_memory=False`.

---

### 🔴 Bug 3 — Silent NA-mask divergence (wrong data, no error)

This is the most concerning: no exception, wrong values. NA tokens are kept as literal strings instead of NA when a chunk contains only `{NA-token} + {int in [2⁶³, 2⁶⁴-1]}`.

```python
import pandas as pd

OVER = "9223372036854775808"  # 2**63
with open("f3.csv", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("c0\nabc\n")
    fh.write("\n".join("nan" if i % 5 == 0 else OVER for i in range(4_000_000)))  # ~64 MB
    fh.write("\n")

par = pd.read_csv("f3.csv", low_memory=False)
with pd.option_context("mode.max_threads", 1):
    ser = pd.read_csv("f3.csv", low_memory=False)

ser["c0"].isna().sum()   # 800000  (all "nan" -> NA)
par["c0"].isna().sum()   # 200000  (600000 "nan" kept as the literal string "nan")
```

Both columns have dtype `str`, so the per-column dtype reconciliation (`_read_csv_parallel`, which compares only `dtype.kind`) sees `str == str` and concatenates without falling back.

**Mechanism.** A chunk of only `{NA-token, uint64-range int}` overflows int64 → retries uint64 → hits `uint64_conflict` (`seen_uint && seen_null`) → routed to the "leave AS IS" branch in `_convert_tokens`, which calls `_string_convert(..., na_filter=0, ...)` (`parsers.pyx` ~L1139 / ~L1147) and emits NA tokens literally. The whole-file serial read also contains `abc`, so it takes the object branch with the real `na_filter` and masks NA. This affects default NA tokens **and** custom `na_values` (list and dict), under object/`str`/pyarrow/`numpy_nullable`. It does **not** affect empty strings, bool+NA, values that overflow uint64, or `keep_default_na=False`.

**Note on the fix:** the `na_filter=0` "AS IS" emission is intentional and tested (`test_na_values_uint64`, GH-14983 asserts uint64-conflict columns are kept literal), so this can't be fixed by simply passing `na_filter` through — that reverts GH-14983. The parallel-specific regression should instead be addressed by respecting `low_memory=False` (see below). The default `low_memory=True` case can't be made byte-identical to a whole-file read without giving up parallelism, since serial `low_memory` already gives context-dependent NA here — probably a doc note.

---

### Lower-severity

- **Bug 4 — inconsistent error *type* for incompatible explicit `dtype`.** `dtype={"c": "Int64"}` on a column of mixed float/overflow-int can raise `OverflowError` from the parallel path vs `TypeError` from serial. Both fail; only the message differs. It is deterministic (the first chunk's error propagates via ordered `future.result()`), not a thread race.
- **Bug 5 — duplicated warnings from worker threads.** A converter+dtype `ParserWarning` fires once per chunk from the `ThreadPoolExecutor` workers (serial: 1, parallel: N), with a racy `stacklevel`.
- **Bug 6 — mmap unmap deferred on the error path.** When a worker raises anything other than `ParserError`/`UnicodeDecodeError`, its traceback pins the memoryview, so `mm.close()` raises `BufferError` and is suppressed; the mapping is unmapped only when the traceback is GC'd (transient address-space/FD hold). Bug 1 and Bug 2 both exercise this path.

---

### Suggested fixes

1. **Bug 1** — catch `EmptyDataError` in name inference → `return None`.
2. **`low_memory=False` gate** — `if kwds.get("low_memory") is False: return False` in `_can_parallelize_csv`. This removes the parallel-specific part of both **Bug 2** and **Bug 3** for callers who opted out of chunked inference. (Validated: they fall back and match, 78 tests pass.)
3. **Bug 2** under default `low_memory` — additionally gate `dtype_backend="pyarrow"` or fall back when a pyarrow int chunk exceeds 2⁵³.
4. **Bug 5 / Bug 6** — polish; Bug 6 is roughly a one-liner.

### Verified solid (no divergence found)

Thread/memory safety under a 250×-repeat concurrency stress (byte-identical every run; the SIMD tokenizer scan never over-reads past the mmap end); quoted embedded newlines (a boundary inside a quote always leaves a chunk mid-quote → `EOF inside string` → fallback, incl. a 50k-embedded-newline field spanning 16 chunks); the byte-offset/chunk-boundary math (1-row × 16-worker, multibyte headers, giant lines, huge preambles); `dtype="category"`, `encoding_errors`, BOM/CRLF/no-trailing-newline, thousands/decimal, uint64+NA precision, and wide/multi-column reads.

Not tested here (would need a different environment): free-threaded (no-GIL) builds, Windows/Linux specifics.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd

left = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 5, 10], "left_val": ["a", "b", "c"]})
right = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 6, 10], "right_val": ["A", "B", "C"]})

# tolerance=0 is accepted and meaningful: exact-match-only
print(pd.merge_asof(left, right, on="a", tolerance=0))
#     a left_val right_val
# 0   1        a         A
# 1   5        b       NaN   <- no exact match within 0
# 2  10        c         C

# but a negative tolerance is rejected with a message that claims 0 is invalid too:
pd.merge_asof(left, right, on="a", tolerance=-1)
# MergeError: tolerance must be positive
```

### Issue Description

`merge_asof` accepts `tolerance=0` (which means exact-match-only, a meaningful asof semantic), but the error raised for an invalid `tolerance` says it `must be positive`. The three guards in `_MergeOperation`/`_AsOfMerge` reject only strictly-negative values:

```python
if self.tolerance < Timedelta(0):
    raise MergeError("tolerance must be positive")
...
if self.tolerance < 0:
    raise MergeError("tolerance must be positive")
```

So `0` is accepted, yet "must be positive" (which means `> 0`) excludes it. The message is inconsistent with the guard.

### Expected Behavior

The message should say `tolerance must be non-negative`, matching the values the guard actually accepts.

<details>

Reproduced on `main` and pandas 3.0.3.

I [the human] asked Claude to post the following:

## Summary

When a DataFrame has a MultiIndex with `nlevels == ndim` (the most common case: a 2-level MI on a 2D DataFrame), tuple keys passed to `.loc` are fundamentally ambiguous between two interpretations:

1. **MI row key**: `df.loc[(a, b)]` means "the row with MultiIndex key `(a, b)`"
2. **Multi-axis indexing**: `df.loc[a, b]` means "row `a`, column `b`"

Python produces the same tuple `(a, b)` for both spellings. The current code resolves this ambiguity differently depending on context — getitem vs setitem, existing vs missing key, scalar vs slice — leading to a cluster of related bugs where the same syntax silently produces different results.

## Related issues

### Primary — same root ambiguity

| Issue | Status | Problem |
|-------|--------|---------|
| #14969 | Open | `df.loc[0, 0]` returns a DataFrame or a Series depending on the dtype of the inner MI level — identical syntax, different interpretation |
| #16396 | Open | `df.loc[1, 2]` uses the MI interpretation, but `df.loc[:1, 2]` and `df.loc[:, 2]` switch to multi-axis (column `2`) — incoherent |
| #27248 | Open | `df.loc[(1, 2019)] = [3, 4]` fails on setitem-with-expansion because the MI key `(1, 2019)` is misinterpreted as `(row=1, col=2019)` |
| #42603 | Open | `df.loc["foo", 0]` silently returns different things depending on whether `0` exists in MI level 1 — proposes an ambiguity error |
| #19110 | Open | `df.loc[existing_row, new_col] = val` adds a column instead of a (partial) row — missing-label priority is inconsistent with present-label priority |
| #17024 | Open | `df.loc['all'] = [5, 6]` on a MI DataFrame flattens the MI to tupled strings |

### See also

| Issue | Status | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| #39775 | Open | KeyError semantics for partially-missing MI keys in slices — adjacent problem about what should happen when MI keys don't exist |
| #16018 | Closed | `cannot reindex from duplicate axis` on MI expansion (fixed in 1.3) |
| #22247 | Closed | MI expansion with NaN level copies wrong values (fixed) |

## Current behavior

### The resolution rule depends on context

The current code applies different heuristics depending on the operation and key type:

**getitem with scalar tuple** (`_getitem_lowerdim` → `_handle_lowerdim_multi_index_axis0`):
- Try MI key via `obj.xs(tup)`. If found → return row.
- If `KeyError` and `ndim < len(tup) <= nlevels` → re-raise (MI interpretation).
- If `KeyError` and `len(tup) == nlevels == ndim` → raise `IndexingError`, which is suppressed by the caller so the per-axis loop handles it as multi-axis.

This means getitem **silently switches interpretation** when a MI key is missing:

```python
mi = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([(1, 2), (3, 4)])
df = pd.DataFrame([[10, 20], [30, 40]], index=mi, columns=[100, 200])

df.loc[(1, 2)]    # → Series (MI row key found)
df.loc[(1, 100)]  # → Series (MI key not found → silently becomes row=1, col=100)
```

**getitem with slices** (`_getitem_tuple_same_dim`):
- Always multi-axis. `df.loc[:1, 2]` treats `2` as a column, even though `df.loc[1, 2]` treats it as MI level 1 (#16396).

**setitem with scalar tuple** (`_get_setitem_indexer`):
- Try MI key via `ax.get_loc(key)`. If found → overwrite row.
- If `KeyError` → suppress, fall through to `_convert_tuple` (always multi-axis). This is why #27248 fails — the missing MI key is reinterpreted as `(row, new_column)`.

### The result depends on dtype

Because the fallback to multi-axis only triggers when the MI lookup fails, and whether it finds a match depends on what values are in the MI levels, the **same syntax gives different results depending on dtype** (#14969):

```python
# String inner level → (0, 0) is NOT in the MI (level 1 is strings),
# so MI lookup fails and multi-axis takes over: partial level-0 key
# on both axes yields a DataFrame.
ind = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([[0, 1], ['A', 'B']])
df = pd.DataFrame(..., index=ind, columns=ind)
df.loc[0, 0]  # → DataFrame

# Int inner level → (0, 0) IS in the MI, so MI row lookup succeeds
# and returns that single row as a Series (indexed by the column MI).
ind = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([[0, 1], [0, 1]])
df = pd.DataFrame(..., index=ind, columns=ind)
df.loc[0, 0]  # → Series
```

## Cases that already work

The ambiguity only exists when `nlevels == ndim`. These cases work correctly:

- **Series with MI** (`ndim=1`): any tuple with `len > 1` exceeds ndim, so `_convert_tuple` raises `IndexingError("Too many indexers")` and the fallthrough correctly handles MI keys.
- **3+-level MI on DataFrame** (`nlevels > ndim=2`): same mechanism — `_convert_tuple` rejects the tuple and the fallthrough handles it.

## Why heuristics don't work

I explored several heuristic approaches to disambiguate setitem when `nlevels == ndim`:

1. **Check if last element is an existing column**: Fails for `df.loc[partial_key, new_col] = val` (simultaneous row + column expansion).
2. **Check type compatibility of each element with its MI level**: Fails when MI levels and columns share the same dtype (e.g., int/int MI + int columns).
3. **Combined type + column-dtype check**: Handles many cases but is fundamentally a guess — there exist DataFrames where both interpretations are type-valid.

The ambiguity is inherent to the API, not a deficiency in the implementation.

## The right API

I think the right long-term answer is: **`.loc` should not guess**. When `nlevels == ndim`, there should be one canonical interpretation, and the user should use explicit syntax for the other.

### Option A: MI key always wins

`.loc[(a, b)]` on a 2-level MI always means MI row key. Multi-axis indexing requires the explicit `df.loc[(a, b), :]` form (or partial keys like `df.loc[a, col]` when `a` is clearly a single level-0 value).

**Pros**: Consistent with getitem priority (MI key is tried first). Consistent with Series. The multi-axis form `df.loc[..., :]` is explicit and readable.

**Cons**: Behavior change for `df.loc[scalar, col]` when the scalar matches level 0 and `col` matches a column.

### Option B: Multi-axis always wins

`.loc[(a, b)]` on a 2-level MI always means `(row=a, col=b)`. MI row key indexing requires `df.loc[pd.IndexSlice[a, b]]` or `df.loc[(a, b), :]`.

**Pros**: No behavior change for existing multi-axis code. Consistent with how `_convert_tuple` already works.

**Cons**: Breaks `df.loc[(a, b)]` for MI row access, which is arguably the more natural reading. Inconsistent with Series and with the `nlevels > ndim` case.

### Option C: Raise on ambiguity

When `nlevels == ndim` and the key is a plain tuple, raise an error (as suggested in #42603) requiring the user to be explicit. Problem: Python offers no way to distinguish `df.loc[(a, b)]` from `df.loc[a, b]`, so we'd have to reject *all* plain tuple keys when `nlevels == ndim`, which is extremely disruptive.

### My recommendation: Option A

The key observation is that the MI-key interpretation is already the **first thing tried** in both getitem and setitem — the multi-axis path is always a fallback. Making the MI-key interpretation authoritative (rather than a try/except heuristic) would make the behavior predictable and consistent across getitem, setitem, scalars, and slices.

Users who need multi-axis indexing on a 2-level MI DataFrame can write `df.loc[(a, b), :]` or use `pd.IndexSlice`.

## How to get there

1. **Short term**: Document the ambiguity and the `df.loc[(a, b), :]` workaround in the MultiIndex docs.
2. **Medium term**: Add a `FutureWarning` when the ambiguous case is hit — when `nlevels == ndim`, MI key lookup fails, and the code is about to fall back to multi-axis. The warning should suggest explicit syntax.
3. **Long term**: Change the default to MI key interpretation when `nlevels == ndim`, removing the multi-axis fallback.

This would resolve #27248, #19110, #16396, #42603, and #14969. #17024 (MI flattening on scalar expansion) is a separate sub-bug in the expansion machinery.

### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the main branch of pandas.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd

mi = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([("a", 1), ("b", 2)], names=["l", "n"])
mi.set_levels([["x", "y"]], level=0)
```

### Issue Description

`MultiIndex.set_levels` (and `set_codes`) raise a self-contradictory message when a **single, scalar** `level` is paired with a **nested** (list-of-lists) value:

```
TypeError: Levels must be list-like
```

The value `[["x", "y"]]` *is* list-like — that's precisely why control reaches this branch. In `_require_listlike` (`pandas/core/indexes/multi.py`), the scalar-level branch first rejects a non-list-like `arr` with `"must be list-like"`, and then rejects a *nested* `arr` (a list of lists) with the **same** string, which is a copy-paste of the first message:

```python
if level is not None and not is_list_like(level):
    if not is_list_like(arr):
        raise TypeError(f"{arrname} must be list-like")          # arr is not list-like — message correct
    if len(arr) > 0 and is_list_like(arr[0]):
        raise TypeError(f"{arrname} must be list-like")          # arr IS list-like (nested) — message wrong
```

For a scalar level the value must be a *flat* list-like, so the second message should say that, not repeat "must be list-like".

### Expected Behavior

The nested-value case should raise a message that names the real constraint, e.g.:

```
TypeError: Levels must be list-like, not a list of lists-like
```

which mirrors the existing `"must be list of lists-like"` message used for the list-valued `level` branch.

### Installed Versions

<details>

main branch (`_require_listlike` in `pandas/core/indexes/multi.py`).

</details>
title: BUG: MultiIndex.set_levels/set_codes give self-contradictory "must be list-like" error for a nested value with a scalar level

### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/development/contributing_environment.html) of pandas.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "random1": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0],
        "random2": [10, 20, 30, 40],
        "type": ["a", "a", "b", "b"],
    }
)

# aggfunc only covers "random1"; "random2" is picked up implicitly via `values`
df.pivot_table(index="type", aggfunc={"random1": "mean"}, margins=True)
```

### Issue Description

Raises:

```
KeyError: 'random2'
```

Without `margins=True`, the exact same call works fine and silently excludes `random2` from the result (since it isn't a key in the `aggfunc` dict):

```python
>>> df.pivot_table(index="type", aggfunc={"random1": "mean"})
      random1
type
a         1.5
b         3.5
```

This also reproduces when `values` is passed explicitly and includes a column not covered by the dict:

```python
df.pivot_table(index="type", values=["random1", "random2"], aggfunc={"random1": "mean"}, margins=True)
```

The root cause seems to be in `_compute_grand_margin` in `pandas/core/reshape/pivot.py`: it iterates over every column in `data[values]` and looks up `aggfunc[k]` for each one. When `aggfunc` is a dict that doesn't have a key for `k`, this will raise a `KeyError`, which propagates uncaught (only `TypeError` is currently swallowed there). I guess the fix is to skip columns not present in the dict, consistent with the non-margins aggregation path's existing (if implicit) behavior of silently dropping such columns.

I found as an incidental, separate issue while investigating and trying to fix #12210 on my own (dict `aggfunc` containing a list of functions per column + `margins=True`). However, this is a distinct root cause/code path and reproduces independently of list-vs-scalar functions.

### Expected Behavior

`margins=True` should produce the same set of columns as `margins=False` (i.e. silently drop columns the `aggfunc` dict doesn't cover), rather than raising `KeyError`.

### Installed Versions

main branch (post `84d7518bdc`)
title: BUG: `pivot_table` with `margins=True` raises KeyError when dict aggfunc doesn't cover every aggregated column

### Issue Summary This is an extremely elusive and odd issue... but using the Database Search Backend with MySQL, *some* particular search queries return no results when paginated, but DO return results when not paginated. The issue is only exhibited when filtering using `.type()` on the `Page` queryset, and only for page types which have multi-level inheritance from `Page`. The issue only occurs with MySQL, not with SQLite or Postgres. This bug very heavily affects the wagtail admin search. https://github.com/wagtail/wagtail/assets/13453401/003d6797-3f43-416f-a5e8-744a436b060d ### Steps to Reproduce Start with a fresh wagtail project: ``` wagtail start brokensearch ``` Then Add some models as so to `home/models.py`: ```python from django.db import models from wagtail.models import Page class BasePage(Page): is_creatable = False class HomePage(BasePage): pass class ThirdPage(HomePage): pass ``` Next modify the boilerplate search view `search/views.py`: ```python from django.core.paginator import EmptyPage, PageNotAnInteger, Paginator from django.template.response import TemplateResponse from django.contrib.contenttypes.models import ContentType from wagtail.models import Page from home.models import ThirdPage def search(request): search_query = request.GET.get("query", None) page = request.GET.get("page", 1) # Search if search_query: results = Page.objects.live() # search_results = results.search(search_query) search_results = results.type(ThirdPage).search(search_query) else: search_results = Page.objects.none() # Pagination paginator = Paginator(search_results, 10) try: search_results = paginator.page(page) except PageNotAnInteger: search_results = paginator.page(1) except EmptyPage: search_results = paginator.page(paginator.num_pages) return TemplateResponse( request, "search/search.html", { "search_query": search_query, "search_results": search_results, }, ) ``` Next modify the boilerplate `search/templates/search/search.html` template: ```jinja {% extends "base.html" %} {% load static wagtailcore_tags %} {% block body_class %}template-searchresults{% endblock %} {% block title %}Search{% endblock %} {% block content %}

Search

Non-Paginated

{% for result in search_results.paginator.object_list %}

{{ result }}

{% endfor %}

Paginated

{% for result in search_results %}

{{ result }}

{% endfor %} {% endblock %} ``` Next, be sure to set the database to MySQL (this can be changed later on to compare results between SQLite, Postgres) in `settings/dev.py`: ```python DATABASES = { "default": { "ENGINE": "django.db.backends.mysql", "HOST": "localhost", "NAME": "brokensearch", "USER": "root", "PASSWORD": "", "OPTIONS": { "charset": "utf8mb4", }, } } ``` Next, delete the existing migrations, make and apply migrations: ``` rm -r home/migrations/ python manage.py makemigrations home python manage.py migrate ``` Create a superuser, log in to wagtail, and DELETE the "Welcome to your new Wagtail site!" page. From this screen, click "Add child page" and create a page of type `HomePage` named "Home". Next, go to Settings > Site and create a new site, using the newly created Home page as the root. Next, create a `ThirdPage`, as a child of "Home", with the EXACT title below: ``` Third page blog ``` Now go to http://localhost:8000/search/. If you enter the search term "Third", it will return the result under both non-paginated and paginated sections. The same thing will happen if you search "page" or "blog". So everything works. Now - to break the search - create another page, this time of type `HomePage` in the wagtail admin, also as a child of "Home" (a sibling of "Third page blog") with the EXACT title below: ``` Home page blog ``` Once again, go to http://localhost:8000/search/. If you enter the search term "Third", it will return the result under both non-paginated and paginated sections. BUT if you search for "page" or "blog", you will no longer get the result under the paginated results!!! To further prove our results, let's manually update the search index: ``` python manage.py update_index ``` Repeat the previous step, searching for "Third", and "page", and "blog". The broken results persist. Yet another proof of the search results: in the Wagtail admin, beneath the wagtail logo, search for "blog". The results are as expected. However, if you filter by Page type: "Third page (1)", the search results completely disappear. ### Technical details - Python version: 3.11.6 - Django version: Tested with every single dot release from 3.2.0 to 4.2.7 - Wagtail version: Tested with every single dot release from 4.2.0 to 5.2.1 - Browser version: N/A - MySQL server version: 8.0.33 (tested under both Windows and Linux) - mysqlclient: 2.2.0, tested with versions compiled with MariaDB C connector and MySQL 8.0.33 C Connector. ### Working on this The first step will be to reproduce the issue. See the comments below.

### Problem statement

We have a lot of various scripts/tasks and variations thereof we use when working on Wagtail. I’m starting to feel like we need a more advanced one than make / Makefile, to reduce friction.

### Proposed solution

Switch to [just](https://github.com/casey/just) / justfile, as a replacement for make / [our Makefile](https://github.com/wagtail/wagtail/blob/main/Makefile). It’s similar enough in behavior that the transition should be smooth, but has key advantages that are very relevant for us:

- Support for documenting commands/recipes with comments
- Command groups that are very helpful for documentation / ease of use
- Command arguments

Switching to Just, I expect we would:

- Replace our current Makefile 1:1
- Integrate some of the scripts from our package.json
- Integrate some of the scripts from the separate `docs/Makefile`
- Integrate frequently-used scripts currently only mentioned in docs
- TBC: Integrate some of the options of `runtests.py`

### Alternative solutions

just / justfile isn’t massively different to Makefiles, so some of the changes proposed above could also be achieved while staying on Make. However we’d have to be creating a bespoke system around the commands to organize them better, that wouldn’t scale as well.

### Additional context

See [cookiecutter-wagtail-package justfile](https://github.com/wagtail/cookiecutter-wagtail-package/blob/main/justfile) as an example.

### Working on this

This needs feedback from our maintainers, and is likely better done by an established maintainer if we agree to proceed.
title: Switch from make / Makefile to just / justfile

Part of [RFC 115](https://wagtail.org/rfc-115/), tracked in #14295.

## Problem statement

[RFC 115 §QA capabilities](https://wagtail.org/rfc-115/#qa-capabilities) defines cross-cutting QA mechanisms. The critical-path pieces (permissions-matrix harness, audit-log assertion helpers, OpenAPI snapshot tooling) moved to #14296. Two RFC items remain unowned: **more advanced fixtures** — extending `wagtail/test/` with content shapes broad enough to exercise the API end-to-end (e.g. custom log models, which existing test apps cover only thinly) — and **automated test case generation** via schema-driven property tests/fuzzing.

## Proposed solution

- [ ] Fixture expansion in `wagtail/test/`: review gaps against the API tickets' needs (custom log models, deeper translated trees, collection permission scenarios); extend `testapp` rather than adding apps where possible.
- [ ] Property tests / fuzzing (best-effort, RFC marks it "if possible"): generate request payloads from the exported JSON Schemas (e.g. `hypothesis` + `hypothesis-jsonschema`); assert no 500s, and RFC 7807 conformance on rejection. Time-box; document findings either way.

## Acceptance criteria / definition of done

- Fixture additions documented per existing test-app conventions, and consumed by at least one endpoint ticket's tests.
- Property-test outcome documented: running in CI (possibly non-blocking) or a written conclusion on why not.

Suggested review steps:

1. Run the property tests locally overnight against the v3 branch; triage anything found.
2. Check `runtests.py` time impact stays acceptable.

## Additional context

- RFC 115: [QA capabilities — Core](https://wagtail.org/rfc-115/#core).
- Property tests need #14296's schema export; fixture work has no blocker.

## Working on this

Assignee TBC. Effort: not in the RFC effort matrix — estimate S–M (~8–12h).
title: Write API: QA fixtures and property testing

body_text:
### Problem statement

The image and document edit templates do not provide a dedicated template block for the metadata/stats section that displays information such as filesize and usage.

When projects need to add a small piece of additional metadata to this section, for example an "Uploaded by" field, they currently have to override and copy the entire template. This creates unnecessary maintenance overhead and increases the risk of diverging from upstream Wagtail templates as they evolve.

A separate package, `wagtailmedia`, has a comparable [edit template](https://github.com/torchbox/wagtailmedia/blob/main/src/wagtailmedia/templates/wagtailmedia/media/edit.html) that wraps this kind of metadata section in a `media_stats` block. While this is not part of Wagtail core, it demonstrates the type of extension point that would be useful for Wagtail’s built-in image and document edit templates.

### Proposed solution

Add dedicated template blocks around the metadata/stats sections in the image and document edit templates.

For example:

```django
{% block document_stats %}
    ...
{% endblock %}
```

in `wagtaildocs/documents/edit.html`, and:

```django
{% block image_stats %}
    ...
{% endblock %}
```

in `wagtailimages/images/edit.html`.

This would allow projects to extend or customise the metadata displayed alongside the edit form without needing to override the entire template. Existing behaviour would remain unchanged, while providing a more maintainable extension point for downstream projects.

### Alternative solutions

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Working on this

I'd be happy to work on this if the proposal is accepted.

I've already implemented a similar customisation on a Wagtail project where I needed to add additional metadata ("Uploaded by") to the image and document edit views. As part of that work, I've identified the relevant templates and have a working example of the proposed approach.

The change should be relatively small, consisting of introducing dedicated template blocks around the existing metadata sections while preserving the current behaviour.
title: Wrap stats section in a block to the `edit.html` for image ands documents.

For example to declare the language on specific words: #4694. [RFC 46: Single paragraph rich text fields/blocks](https://github.com/wagtail/rfcs/pull/46) has been accepted, so this can now proceed. This is to implement "single-line" rich text server-side, integrating with the relevant Wagtail and Django APIs (DB storage format, rich text diffing, search, translations, etc.) ### Tasks Done in #7249 as a WIP implementation: - [x] [`mutliline=false` support in Draftail](https://www.draftail.org/docs/formatting-options#single-line-support) - [ ] DB field - [ ] Support in ContentState converters - [ ] Widget incl. template - [ ] Widget Telepath adapter - [ ] StreamField block Other tasks: - [ ] Comparison support (diffing) - [ ] Search support - [ ] References support - [ ] Comments support ## Working on this This feature is [on the Wagtail roadmap](https://wagtail.org/roadmap/) in the "Future" area. We’re looking for a feature sponsor for this, to cover the cost of completing the WIP work at #7249. Alternatively, this can be picked up by any contributor, continuing from #7249. If you’re interested in sponsoring this feature or working on it please let us know.
title: Single-line RichTextField

body_text:
### Issue summary

`Vector.__repr__` and `Rect.__repr__` in `wagtail/images/rect.py` use `%d`
(integer format), which silently truncates float values to integers.

Methods like `_set_size()` and `_set_centroid()` use float division, so
coordinates are frequently floats. This makes debugging misleading:

```python
v = Vector(1.7, 3.9)
repr(v)  # returns "Vector(x: 1, y: 3)" instead of "Vector(x: 1.7, y: 3.9)"

The fix is to use f-strings, consistent with the rest of the codebase
(e.g. list_block.py, formats.py).
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Django shell in a Wagtail project: `python manage.py shell`
2. Run the following:

```python
from wagtail.images.rect import Rect, Vector

# Vector with float values
v = Vector(1.7, 3.9)
print(repr(v))  # prints "Vector(x: 1, y: 3)" — wrong

# Rect with float coords via set_size (uses float division)
r = Rect(0, 0, 10, 10)
r.size = Vector(7, 7)
print(repr(r))  # prints "Rect(left: 1, top: 1, right: 9, bottom: 9)" — wrong
```

### Additional information

No response

### Can be reproduced

Yes, on a fresh Wagtail project

### Technical details

- Python version: Run `python --version`.
- Django version: Look in your requirements.txt, or run `pip show django | grep Version`.
- Wagtail version: Look at the bottom of the Settings menu in the Wagtail admin, or run `pip show wagtail | grep Version:`.
- Browser version: You can use https://www.whatsmybrowser.org/ to find this out.


### Working on this

If you would like to contribute to this issue, follow these steps:
- Confirm that the issue is reproducible, either on a fresh Wagtail project or the [bakerydemo](https://github.com/wagtail/bakerydemo).
- Once confirmed, view our [contributing guidelines](https://docs.wagtail.org/en/latest/contributing/index.html), add a comment to the issue once you're ready to start.
title: Vector and Rect __repr__ silently truncates float coordinates

body_text:
### Issue summary

When a page has an inline child model (via `ParentalKey`) that carries a `UniqueConstraint` across two of its fields, saving a draft can raise a `500 IntegrityError` if the form submits a child entry without a PK while a committed row for the same field combination already exists in the database.

The error thrown:

```
IntegrityError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "unique_blog_person"
DETAIL: Key (page_id, person_id)=(84, 1) already exists.
```

It is raised inside `wagtail.admin.views.pages.edit.EditView` (and equivalently in the snippet edit view for `DraftStateMixin` models).

The id-less entry arises in two ways:

1. **Autosave / concurrent-tab race.** Tab A adds a child object and autosave commits it to the database. Tab B loaded the form before that commit and still has an empty `id` field for the same object. When Tab B saves, modelcluster sees no PK, issues an `INSERT`, and Postgres rejects it.

2. **DraftStateMixin publish unpublish cycle.** For snippet models using `DraftStateMixin`, draft saves use `commit=False`, so the through-model row is never written to the database and the revision JSON therefore lacks a PK. Publishing commits the row. Unpublishing causes `get_latest_revision_as_object()` to fall back to that revision (because `has_unpublished_changes=True`), restoring the id-less state. The next save then hits the same `INSERT` conflict.

A minimal reproduction using `bakerydemo` (adding a `UniqueConstraint` to the `BlogPersonRelationship` through model) and a working fix are demonstrated in [this pr](https://github.com/wagtail/bakerydemo/pull/762). The bug was initial found in [ONSdigital/dis-wagtail#697](https://github.com/ONSdigital/dis-wagtail/pull/697).

**Current Workaround / Fix**

Override save() on the through model to detect an id-less INSERT that would duplicate an existing row, look up the existing PK, and flip _state.adding = False so Django issues an UPDATE instead:

```python
def save(self, **kwargs):
    if (
        not kwargs.get("force_insert")
        and self._state.adding
        and self.page_id
        and self.person_id
    ):
        existing_pk = (
            BlogPersonRelationship.objects.filter(
                page_id=self.page_id, person_id=self.person_id
            )
            .values_list("pk", flat=True)
            .first()
        )
        if existing_pk is not None:
            self.pk = existing_pk
            self._state.adding = False
    super().save(**kwargs)
```

### Steps to reproduce


These steps use the `ParentalKey` + `UniqueConstraint` pattern. A minimal reproduction can be see on this [bakery demo pr](https://github.com/wagtail/bakerydemo/pull/762)

**Setup** 

Add a `UniqueConstraint` to an existing `ParentalKey` through model, e.g.:

```python
class BlogPersonRelationship(Orderable, models.Model):
    page = ParentalKey("BlogPage", related_name="blog_person_relationship", on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    person = models.ForeignKey("base.Person", on_delete=models.CASCADE)

    class Meta(Orderable.Meta):
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(fields=["page", "person"], name="unique_blog_person"),
        ]
```

#### Autosave / two-tab race (reproduces on any Page type):

1. Create a page that uses the through model above, save as draft, open the edit URL in Tab A and Tab B simultaneously.
2. In Tab A: add a child object (e.g. an author) and wait for autosave to fire. The through-model row is now committed to the database.
3. In Tab B: add the same child object (the form still has an empty id field because it was loaded before Tab A's autosave). Click Save draft.
4. Observe: 500 IntegrityError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint.

#### Publish unpublish cycle (reproduces on DraftStateMixin snippet models):

1. Publish a page/snippet that has the through model.
2. Edit it, add a child object, and Save draft (commits no row, commit=False).
3. Publish (commits the through-model row with a real PK).
4. Unpublish (sets has_unpublished_changes=True; the edit form now loads via get_latest_revision_as_object(), latest_revision.as_object(), which contains the id-less revision data).
5. Save draft throws 500 IntegrityError.

### Additional information


This is a bug rather than a misconfiguration because:

- `UniqueConstraint` on a `ParentalKey` through model is a documented pattern. Nothing in the Wagtail docs warns that adding one will make the admin unsafe under concurrent edits or publish/unpublish cycles.
- The failure mode is a silent `500` with no user-facing recovery. The editor loses their work and has no indication of what went wrong.
- The constraint itself is correct, the duplicate entry is the problem, not the constraint. Wagtail (via modelcluster) should handle deduplication gracefully rather than letting an `INSERT` race reach the database.

**Expected behaviour:** if an id-less child entry is submitted for a `(page, child)` combination that already has a committed row, Wagtail should recognise the existing row and update it rather than attempting a duplicate insert.

A model-level workaround exists (see Steps to reproduce), fix is likely in `modelcluster` itself, either by catching `IntegrityError` and retrying as an update, or by consulting the model's `Meta.constraints` before issuing the insert.

### Can be reproduced

Yes, on the bakerydemo

### Technical details

- **Python version:** 3.12.13
- **Django version:** 6.0.6
- **Wagtail version:** 7.4.2
- **django-modelcluster version:** 6.5
- **Database:** PostgreSQL 18.1
- **Browser:** n/a (reproduces via any browser / direct POST)

### Working on this

_No response_
title: IntegrityError on draft save when ParentalKey through model has UniqueConstraint and a concurrent or stale form submission produces an id-less child entry

body_text: ### Issue summary When no sites are configured in Wagtail (Settings → Sites is empty), opening the URL Generator for any image crashes with: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'root_url' This happens in `wagtail/images/views/images.py` in `get_context_data`. The code falls back to `Site.objects.first()` when no default site exists, but does not handle the case where no sites exist at all, causing `.root_url` to be called on `None`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Go to Settings → Sites and delete all sites 2. Go to Images → click any image → Edit 3. Click "URL Generator" 4. The page crashes with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'root_url' ### Additional information _No response_ ### Can be reproduced Not confirmed ### Technical details - Python version: Run `python --version`. - Django version: Look in your requirements.txt, or run `pip show django | grep Version`. - Wagtail version: Look at the bottom of the Settings menu in the Wagtail admin, or run `pip show wagtail | grep Version:`. - Browser version: You can use https://www.whatsmybrowser.org/ to find this out. ### Working on this I have reproduced this issue on the bakerydemo and I am planning to work on a fix.

body_text:
### Problem statement

As part of regular security report handling and one-off reports like [Independent security audit - report highlights](https://github.com/wagtail/wagtail/discussions/14173), there are a few recurring themes where I think it’d help us a lot to better document what we do. Potentially adopt more advanced processes / tooling.

### Proposed solution

Those are just ideas and each might warrant its own ticket - starting the list to get feedback. #14287 might also help us come up with more valuable improvements.

#### Threat model docs

I think it’d help us to formally write down what security threats we want to design Wagtail to protect against, and which ones we think are out of scope.

See [guidance on Threat Modeling from OWASP](https://owasp.org/www-community/Threat_Modeling) and the [Threat Modeling Manifesto](https://www.threatmodelingmanifesto.org/). Particular hot topics:

- Image generation risks
- Guarantees of separation in multi-team environments (multi-site, multi-section)

##### Vulnerability report triage docs

And-or general runbook of how we handle vulnerabilities. Our current docs are primarily there for reporters, we have nothing for maintainers / contributors. This would include more info on how we repro, assign severity, verify fixes, devise workarounds.

#### SBOM generation

We should document how / why people might want SBOMs for Wagtail releases, and possibly improve the process so it’s more usable. Right now we can generate them via GitHub but it’s not well signposted, and the resulting files contain a lot of our dev/testing/qa dependencies, which isn’t necessarily the right thing to provide.

#### AI skill for audits

Tying some of those things together, I think we should spend more time trialing and eventually running regular audits assisted with AI. That’d help us be more proactive with certain classes of issues (XSS) that often sneak through our stack.

### Alternative solutions

Other ideas welcome!

### Additional context

_No response_

### Working on this

This requires expertise from members of @wagtail/security, or general security / maintainer expertise. I wouldn’t recommend those tasks for new contributors.
title: Security process improvements

## Problem statement

Tracking issue for implementation of [RFC 115](https://wagtail.org/rfc-115/). TL;DR: v3 read+write REST API built on Django Ninja, replacing v2 and admin API + additional CMS operations.

## Proposed solution

One ticket per effort-matrix area. Budget: 125h Thibaud + 125h Sage. Hours use a provisional mapping (XS=4, S=8, M=12, L=24, XL=48) — revise as tickets are scoped.

| Ticket   | Area                                 | Effort    | Blocked by                             |
| :------- | :----------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------- |
| **v8.0** | | | 
| #14296 | ✅ API framework foundations            | L (~24h)  | —                                      |
| #14297 | ✅ Operations layer foundations         | M (~12h)  | —                                      |
| #14300 | ✅ Sites                                | S (~8h)   | #14296                               |
| #14301 | ✅ Redirects (reference write endpoint) | XS (~4h)  | #14296, #14297                     |
| #14299 | ⌛ Permissions foundations              | S (~4h (8)) @laymonage   | —                                      |
| #14307 | Rich text                            | M (~2h) (12) @thibaudcolas  | —                                      |
| #14308 | Markdown support                     | M (~2h) (12) @thibaudcolas  | #14307                               |
| #14304 | Pages + Revisions                    | XL (~30h) (48) @laymonage | #14296, #14297, #14299, #14301 |
| #14298 | Authentication                       | M (~12h) @thibaudcolas | #14296                               |
| #14302 | ⌛ CLI: Python prototype                | S (~2h) (8h) @thibaudcolas   | #14296                               |
| #14306 | Images                               | M (~12h) @thibaudcolas  | #14296, #14298                     |
| #14305 | Translations                         | M (~12h) @laymonage  | #14304                               |
| #14310 | StreamField                          | S (~8h) @thibaudcolas   | #14304, #14307                     |
| #14312 | Snippets                             | M (~12h) @laymonage  | #14304                               |
| **Between releases** | | | 
| #14311 | Documents                            | S (~8h)   | #14306                               |
| #14303 | ✅ CLI: Go prototype                    | M (~1h) 12 | #14296                               |
| #14309 | CLI: MVP                             | M (~12h)  | #14298, #14302, #14303           |
| #14313 | CLI: v1                              | M (~12h)  | #14309                               |
| [headless-preview#80](https://github.com/torchbox/wagtail-headless-preview/issues/80) | Compatibility with v3 API in Wagtail 8.0 | | |
| **v8.1** | | | 
| #14314 | Workflows operations                 | M (~12h)  | #14297, #14304                     |
| #14315 | v2 API deprecation plan              | S (~8h)   | #14304                               |
| #14316 | Internal admin API replacement       | M (~12h)  | #14304                               |
| #14317 | API how-tos documentation            | M (~12h)  | #14296                               |
| #14318 | QA fixtures and property testing     | M (~12h)  | —                                      |

Sequencing: (1) foundations in parallel — API framework + rich text (Thibaud), operations layer + permissions (Sage); (2) redirects as end-to-end reference, then pages + revisions, auth, images, CLI prototypes; (3) the rest, CLI MVP → v1.

Capacity: ~88h (Thibaud) + ~116h (Sage) assigned, ~44h TBC from the effort matrix vs ~46h combined slack — near-zero contingency, and #14315–#14318 add ~44h beyond the matrix (though #14317/#14318 partly absorb docs/test effort already implicit in the endpoint tickets). Something must give: defer past the initial release window, descope elsewhere, or extend the budget. Revisit after foundations land.

### Deferred tasks

#### Functionality

- [ ] Integrate with #14258
- [ ] Filters support (to retrofit: sites, redirects, and more)
  - [ ] Redirects equivalent to `?html_path= lookup` (decide whether to keep v2's redirect-based find idiom or return the object directly).
- [ ] In schemas - confirm whether we want to have default values and-or mark fields as optional vs. required
- [ ] In schemas - confirm whether we would want to override titles to get slightly better text (capitalization)
- [ ] Figure out how you can customize endpoints (override vs. reuse, what are the options)
- [ ] Remove unneeded `Site.clear_site_root_paths_cache` (if we confirm it’s indeed not needed)

#### QA architecture

- [ ] Custom audit-log assertion helpers / actions test class to facilitate actions / Ninja testing (`assertLogs` or something like that?)
- [ ] TBC - custom assertion for successful creation?
- [ ] Permissions-matrix harness (actions x roles)

#### Docs for users

- [ ] How-to docs for essential API features
- [ ] Fix/tweak/replace OpenAPI schema integration in docs
- [ ] Agent skills
- [ ] v8.0 upgrade notes
- [ ] v2 -> v3 migration guide

#### Docs for customisations

- [ ] Actions classes: Document the action contract (`__init__` / `check(skip_permission_checks)` / `execute()` / `log_action` substitution) as a public Python API — basis for the RFC's "programmatic content manipulation in Python" guide.

#### Docs for contributors

- [ ] Draft.js exporter skill
- [ ] Ninja skill
- [ ] Contributor docs for action classes
- [ ] Document the django-shinobi fallback rationale.
- [ ] Permissions policies enforced for admin views vs. APIs

#### Possible refactorings

##### Must

##### Should

- [ ] Remove actions’ support for operating on instances without providing `forms` (as we want to guarantee custom validation is always applied in the API layer)
- [ ] Confirm exposure to possible race conditions in generation of the types / schemas depending on declaration order / initialization order

##### Could

- [ ] Enforce all actions `.execute` comes with a `.check` first by overriding private `_execute` method in subclasses
- [ ] Remove/refactor `get_public_pages_queryset` (V2 / V3 API compat)

##### Would

#### Decisions to revisit

- [ ] Polish notation vs. reverse polish for operation IDs and URL names in route declarations (`list_sites`, `sites_list`)
- [ ] Where schemas live (routers vs. separate files per schema vs. shared)
- [ ] Whether the actions abstraction includes hooks, or whether that is done at the view level
- [ ] Do we want this? Registry so the API layer and packages can enumerate operations per model — informs `POST /{resource}/{id}/actions/{name}/` and `allowed_actions`.
- [ ] stable / experimental endpoint tier annotations.

#### Out of scope / future

- `LockAction` / `UnlockAction`, `RevertToRevisionAction`
- Comments and view-restriction actions (Low priority), workflow transitions (#14314)
- TBC: more refactoring admin views onto the new actions.
- Publish signals

## Additional context

- [RFC 115](https://wagtail.org/rfc-115/) (working copy: `115-write-api.md`)
- Prior art: [`wagtail-write-api`](https://github.com/tomdyson/wagtail-write-api), [`wagtail-ninja`](https://github.com/sinnwerkstatt/wagtail-ninja), [`wagapi`](https://github.com/tomdyson/wagapi), [RFC 15](https://github.com/wagtail/rfcs/blob/main/text/015-revisions-api-revised.md), [#4667](https://github.com/wagtail/wagtail/issues/4667)
- In-repo prior art: nine unused `APIAction` classes in `wagtail/admin/api/actions/`.

## Working on this

@thibaudcolas and @laymonage, tracked via the child tickets above.

body_text:
### Problem statement

We want to assess our current cybersecurity / information security practices as part of readiness for the [EU Cyber Resilience Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act). Ideally this assessment would be relevant for other legal frameworks (like NIST SSDF). This is focused on how we manage Wagtail itself, not the security of websites themselves.

### Proposed solution

Self-certify against the [OpenSSF Best Practices Badge](https://openssf.org/projects/best-practices-badge/) (see [all criteria](https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/criteria), [criteria explanation](https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/criteria_discussion), [criteria statistics](https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/criteria_stats), and [passing rates of all projects to date](https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/project_stats)). The criteria are split in 6 levels:

- [ ] Passing level of the "Metal series"
- [ ] Silver level
- [ ] Gold level
- [ ] [OSPS Baseline](https://openssf.org/projects/osps-baseline/) level 1
- [ ] Baseline level 2
- [ ] Baseline level 3

As part of this self-certification or as an immediate follow-up, we can:

- [ ] Directly make changes to our processes that we think would improve our posture
- [ ] Report back to the community on the results of our assessment
- [ ] Consider whether / how to similarly self-certify or assess other projects in our ecosystem

### Alternative solutions

We haven’t investigated alternative self-certification or assessment options, though this could be nice. Possibly the [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://scorecard.dev/)

### Additional context

See [first draft certification](https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/13090/passing) from @Stormheg.

### Working on this

Contribute to the discussion to help this move forward. Explain your use cases, discuss possible solutions, research how to adapt existing code, or compatibility concerns.

Once others agree with the proposed changes, anyone can contribute to this. View our [contributing guidelines](https://docs.wagtail.org/en/latest/contributing/index.html). Add a comment to the issue to explain what approach you are taking.
title: Self-certification for OpenSSF Best Practices Badge

### Description

Currently, I'm looking a CSS minification warning that looks like this:

```
warnings when minifying css:
▲ [WARNING] Unexpected "{" [css-syntax-error]

    <stdin>:484:1:
      484 │  {
          ╵  ^
```

This is fairly difficult to track down, as the user needs to go one-by-one to try to figure out which module has an open brace on line 484.

Sometimes this is easier to track down, given a class name or a bit of syntax is shown in the warning, like in the following:

```
warnings when minifying css:
▲ [WARNING] Transforming this CSS nesting syntax is not supported in the configured target environment ("chrome87", "edge88", "es2020", "firefox78", "safari14") [unsupported-css-nesting]

    <stdin>:3:19:
      3 │     div[id*='app'] & {
        ╵                    ^

  The nesting transform for this case must generate an ":is(...)" but the configured target environment does not support the ":is" pseudo-class.
```

Position info is again pretty hard to use, but the content is at least something we can grep for without too much trouble.

This particular warning can be reproduced with the following CSS content, if it's helpful:

```css
body {
  h1 {
    div[id*='app'] & {
      color: red;
    }
  }
}
```

Just stick a `<link rel="stylesheet" href"./style.css">` in the HTML entry and you're good to reproduce.

(I fully appreciate this is pretty nasty CSS, I'm working to migrate some old LESS and this is what I'm workin' with at the moment)

### Suggested solution

If possible, a file name in the warning message would be ideal, else, perhaps some more context in the warning, like the line above & below?

body_text:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

In some cases you might have an extra index.html that you want to serve at some nested path, without processing it through Vite. You can put it in a subdirectory of `public`, e.g. `/public/foo/bar/index.html`. However, if you do this, it will only be served at `/foo/bar/index.html`, and crucially not at `/foo/bar/`. This is different from the Webpack dev server, which _will_ serve `index.html` files at the path of their containing directory, which caught me by surprise when migrating from Vue CLI to Vite.

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-944tsu?file=public%2Ffoo%2Fbar%2Findex.html&terminal=dev

### Suggested solution

If a subdirectory inside `public` contains an index.html, the index.html should be served at the path of that directory, either by default or as a configurable option.

### Alternative

Instead of putting the directory in `public`, a possible workaround is to put it in the project root. If you do this it will serve the index file at the directory path. However, this means you need to manually copy the directory over to `dist` afterwards, which is a bit annoying since the whole point of having `public` is to automatically copy over files you don't want processed.

Edit: It's also a bit surprising to me that this behavior differs based on whether it's in `public` or the root

### Describe the bug

We are bundling Svelte components as custom elements using Vite.
We automized this step for a whole bunch of components and every now and then, there might be a component, whose bundle.js leads to conflicts with existing JS code on website we use the components. Worst case so far was a conflict with jQuery, because Vite bundling created a $ var in the global namespace.

There was a workaround PR for this more then a year ago, which does not work with `minify: true`.
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/15489

I describe the problem and my findings in this discussion: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/15489

Usually esbuild wraps everything inside an IIFE to have a scope other than the global scope so minified variables does not conflict. Also esbuild is adding those three to four variables, lets call them helpers.

Vite then again does not take advantage of this IIFE, but instead explicitly set the format option to undefined as stated in this comment: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/5d5508311f9856de69babd72dc4de0e7c21c7ae8/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/esbuild.ts#L281-L290

I think it does so, because it has kind of a multi stage bundling mechanic and the first one already puts an IIFE around the code.

So the old workaround tried to move the variables inside the existing IIFE, but this does not work, when code was minified.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/matths/global-namespace-pollution

### Steps to reproduce

run `npm install` followed my `npm run vite`.
have a look at vite/bundle.js and vite/bundle.min.js and see that there are variables outside the IIFE which might conflict with global variables from other JS packages on the same website.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

`transformIndexHtml()` prints the following error when HTML contains a relative link to a script, and `url` parameter ends in slash (i.e. `/example/dir/`, and not `/example/dir/index.html`):

```console
Pre-transform error: Failed to load url /example/filename.js (resolved id: /example/filename.js). Does the file exist?
```

This can occur when implementing the dev server following the [SSR guide](https://vite.dev/guide/ssr#setting-up-the-dev-server).

### Cause

This happens because `dirname()` of the html url is taken which, for a path that ends in slash, removes the directory name. And the file is searched in the parent directory:
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/63b82f1e29a00d06a82144fd03ea8d6eff114290/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L160-L166

When using builtin vite server, it converts urls that end in slash to absolute filesystem paths that end in index.html:
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/63b82f1e29a00d06a82144fd03ea8d6eff114290/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/htmlFallback.ts#L44-L53

but this doesn't happen for the SSR example since:
1. It uses `appType: 'custom'`, which disables this url preprocessing
2. The custom handler uses `req.originalUrl`, which is not modified
3. The HTML file may not exist

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-dev-vitest-bx1fvf91?file=index.js

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run dev`
3. Observe the error message in console:
```console
Pre-transform error: Failed to load url /example/filename.js (resolved id: /example/filename.js). Does the file exist?
```
4. Ctrl+C
5. Change `/example/dir/` on line 4 to `example/dir/index.html`
6. `npm run dev`
7. Observe no error

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 5.0 undefined
```

### Describe the bug

Vite Config:

```json
{
  "root": "web"
}
```

Project Structure:

```
web
├── index.html
├── main.ts
└── route.ts
```

A request to `/route` will unexpectedly serve `/route.ts`.

Since the file extension is omitted, I would expect for the traditional `connect-history-api-fallback` logic to apply and for `/index.html` to be served. If wanted to load the source file I would expect to have to make an explicit request for `/route.ts`. It doesn't seem right for the file extension to be inferred.

This is likely more of an issue for people like me who've configured `root` since that may mean source files sit at the top-level of `root` instead of nested inside of a `src` directory. Still, for cases such as this, this issue becomes more problematic as more source files and routes are created, since there's more opportunity for an inadvertent conflict.

**Important**: On the first load, you will actually see the correct fallback logic. It's only once vite has processed `route.ts` that the fallback behavior changes, and you'll start seeing a JavaScript file served instead of index.html.

Thanks for your help!

### Describe the bug

After upgrading to Vite@8, I noticed that CSS minification now defaults to Lightning CSS. Since then, production builds started showing warnings or failing when using some modern progressive CSS features that are already supported in browsers.

Examples include selectors and pseudo-elements such as
`::scroll-marker`, `::scroll-marker-group`, `::scroll-button()`, `:target-current`, and `::search-text`.

I also encountered a hard build failure when using `@scope` in a form that currently works in supporting browsers:

```css
@scope (.section) {
  color: blue;
}
```

Switching the CSS minifier back to `esbuild` resolves the issue.

This feels more like a tooling constraint than a platform limitation. Vite has traditionally provided a very standards-friendly developer experience, so it would be great if progressive modern CSS usage remained smooth by default.

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-5gfqfhwc?file=src%2Fstyle.css

Run:

```
npm run build
```

The build fails due to the `@scope` rule being rejected during CSS minification.

Note: the project runs correctly in dev mode, and the CSS works as expected in supporting browsers. The failure only occurs during the production build step.

body_text:
### Description

When integrating Vite with a backend, it is currently cumbersome to reference entry points via their name specified in `build.rollupOptions.input` during development. In production, it's easy thanks to the manifest file, but there is currently no counterpart during development.

Picture the following scenario:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  base: '/static/', // this makes it even more fuzzy
  build: {
    manifest: true,
    rollupOptions: {
      input: {
        main: './frontend/js/main.ts',
        exampleForm: './frontend/js/forms/example.ts',
        nestedDependency: './node_modules/mymodule/process-me.ts' // probably not best practice, but sometimes reality
      }
    },
  },
})
```

Currently, you have to specify the path in the URL of the script to include the assets.

```html
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@vite/client"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/static/frontend/js/main.ts"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/static/frontend/js/forms/example.ts"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/static/node_modules/mymodule/process-me.ts"></script>
```

### Suggested solution

While the above way works, it'd be nicer to be able to reference the entries by their specified name:


```html
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@vite/client"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@entry/main"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@entry/exampleForm"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@entry/nestedDependency"></script>
```

The dev server would simply resolve the entry by its name and redirect accordingly (`http://localhost:5173/@entry/main` → 302 `http://localhost:5173/static/frontend/js/main.ts`)

When moving files around, one would only have to update the Vite config, instead of potentially many references.

### Alternative

- Using plugins such as https://github.com/owlsdepartment/vite-plugin-dev-manifest
- Creating a new third-party plugin which adds the proposed `@entry` routes to the dev server

### Additional context

We're using `django-vite` and have many such lines in our codebase:

```django
{% vite_asset 'frontend/js/forms/example-form.ts' %}
```

This seems much more maintainable to me (but doesn't currently work during development, as it's not possible to get the asset's path from its name):

```django
{% vite_asset 'exampleForm' %}
```

```md
---
id: 6734e2dcb965e5ac0ea38e0f
title: How Can You Build Effective Learning Habits and Work Smarter?
challengeType: 19
dashedName: how-can-you-build-effective-learning-habits-and-work-smarter

# --description--

Read the transcript and answer the questions below.

# --transcript--

To make it through something as rigorous as the freeCodeCamp curriculum, you'll need to not only work hard – you'll need to work smart.

Over the years, I've talked with thousands of people who've learned to code and gotten developer jobs. Here are some tips that have worked for them.

Tip number 1: pace yourself. Learning to code is a marathon, not a sprint. Remember that it's better to code 30 minutes every day of the week, than to try and cram all your learning into one day. This is thanks to the important role that sleep plays in learning.

The freeCodeCamp curriculum already incorporates all those learning concepts I mentioned earlier: spaced repetition, interleaving practice, active recall. All you need to do is sit down and work through the curriculum consistently every day.

This is easier said than done. Most people who start this curriculum will at some point stop. Hopefully, some of those people will come back and finish in the future. But let's talk about you. We want you to finish what you start. And the best advice I have is to remember to pace yourself.

Tip number 2: routine is your friend. If you make a habit of waking up 30 minutes earlier every day, you can get in a coding session before you go to work. After a few weeks of doing this, it just becomes part of your routine. You don't really have to think too much about it, or expend any additional willpower. It's just something that you do.

Now, I understand that you're probably busy. I wish I could tell you that there was just some magic book that you could buy, and that would be enough. The reason buying a book feels so good is that it feels like you're also buying the time to read it. But there's no magic involved in learning to code. You've got to put in the time. You've got to put in the reps at the keyboard. 

I'll tell you this: if you can code for even 30 minutes a day, you're going to make serious gains over the course of a year.

Tip number 3: Use the Pomodoro technique. Pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. In Italy they have these tomato shaped clocks that you set for 25 minutes.

Sitting down to code isn't easy. It takes willpower. So to make it easier to sit down and start that coding, just tell yourself that you're going to code for 25 minutes. Set a timer. Then, once you've finished 25 minutes, you can take a break. But by this point, you may be so deep into your coding session, that you don't even need to take a break.

The Pomodoro technique makes it a lot easier to get started.

Final tip: remember to get plenty of sleep. You'll learn best when you're at your best. Sleep plays a vital role in how your brain learns. I encourage you to try to sleep at least 8 hours each night.

And with that, you're ready to dive into the curriculum and start working toward earning your freeCodeCamp verified certification. Happy coding!
```

body_text:
### Describe the problem

I'm improving my router library.  Now my router can provide hash routing to Sveltekit projects (configured for path routing), so hash routing on top of Sveltekit's path routing.

Since Sveltekit can use regular anchor elements, and because there is at least one styling library (Bulma) that applies the "active" look not to the anchor element, but to the parent `<li>` element, I now want to expose the active feature as an attachment.

My issue:  This is my TS type for the information required for this "active" feature:

```typescript
type ActiveState = {
    key?: string | undefined;
    class?: ClassValue | undefined; // <------------------------   HERE!!!
    style?: HTMLAnchorAttributes["style"] | Record<string, string>;
    ariaCurrent?: HTMLAnchorAttributes["aria-current"];
}
```

I have defined the `class` property as accepting all values accepted by `clsx` because my `<Link>` component simply adds this property value to the array inside the anchor element: `<a ... class={[...., activeState?.class]} ...>`.  Well, in an attachment, I have to do this imperatively with `el.classList`.

### Describe the proposed solution

Allow me to import the `clsx()` function that is built-in in Svelte, so I can do:

```
el.classList.add(clsx(activeState?.class));
```

The alternative would be to explicitly install the `clsx` NPM package, which would be redundant.

### Importance

would make my life easier
title: Make clsx() function available

body_text:
> _Full disclosure: the debugging here was largely done by Claude, reviewed by me (an experienced backend SWE who doesn't know Svelte internals deeply). The bug is real and reproducible._ ## Update — root cause found + minimal repro My original report blamed SvelteKit **remote functions** + `bits-ui`. After extensive bisection those turned out to be **red herrings**. The real trigger is much smaller, and there is now a **dependency-free, pure-Svelte reproduction**: ### ▶ https://github.com/jippi/svelte-batch-roots-repro ```bash pnpm install && pnpm dev # open in Firefox or Chrome, reload a few times ``` ## Summary Under `compilerOptions.experimental.async`, Svelte throws `invariant_violation: "Batch has scheduled roots"` during a layout's **suspense-resolution flush** (the `flushSync` that runs when a top-level `await` settles) when, **in that same flush**: - a component writes a module-level `$state` during its init, and - an **earlier-mounted sibling** is already subscribed to that `$state` through a _rendered_ `$derived`, while - a sibling `{#await}` resolves with a **reactive root** (`{#each}` / `$derived`) in its pending branch. ## Environment - `svelte` **5.56.1**, `@sveltejs/kit` 2.61.1, `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte` 7.1.2, `vite` 8.0.14 - Only non-default flag: `compilerOptions.experimental.async: true` (no `kit.experimental.remoteFunctions`, no third-party deps) - Reproduces in **Firefox and Chromium** — timing race, reliable within ~6 reloads ## The crash ```text Svelte error: invariant_violation "Batch has scheduled roots" at invariant (reactivity/batch.js) at #commit (Batch) at #process (Batch) at flush (Batch) at run_micro_tasks at flushSync at resolve ← an {#await} block resolving ``` The guard is `invariant(batch.#roots.length === 0, 'Batch has scheduled roots')` in `src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js`. ## The whole reproduction ``` svelte.config.js compilerOptions.experimental.async = true (only non-default flag) src/routes/+page.ts export const ssr = false (required: client-flush only) src/lib/shared.svelte.ts export const store = $state({ value: undefined }) src/lib/Reader.svelte const d = $derived(store.value) // mounts FIRST
reader
// ...and must be rendered src/lib/Writer.svelte store.value = 'written' // mounts SECOND, writes during init src/lib/Wrap.svelte let { open, children } = $props() // receives suspended value, never reads it {@render children?.()} src/routes/+layout.svelte let ready = $state(await Promise.resolve(true)) // suspending boundary {@render children?.()} src/routes/+page.svelte const items = [0] const p = new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => r(0), 50)) {#await p}{#each items as n}{n}{/each}{:then s}

{s}

{/await} ``` ## Mechanism (our reading) During the layout's suspense-resolution `flushSync`, the `` subtree — which received the suspended `ready` as a prop — renders. In that single flush: 1. `Reader` mounts and its rendered `$derived` subscribes to `store.value`. 2. `Writer` mounts **after** it and **writes** `store.value` during init, dirtying the Reader's just-created derived **mid-flush**. 3. The sibling page's `{#await}` resolves in the same flush, with a reactive root (`{#each}`) in its pending branch. The overlapping scheduled roots during the batch rebase trip the invariant. Same family as the earlier-fixed #18071 / #18126 / #17940 / #17941 / #17964 / #18221 — this looks like a remaining variant on 5.56.1. ## Necessity map — removing any one stops the crash Each verified in isolation (~6 reloads each): | Requirement | Remove it → | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `compilerOptions.experimental.async` | (premise) | | Layout top-level `await` (suspending boundary) | no crash | | `` **receives the suspended value** as a prop (value unused) | literal / no prop → no crash | | `` wraps Reader **+** Writer **+** the page together | page outside Wrap → no crash | | Two **sibling** components sharing a module `$state` | single self-writing component → no crash | | **Reader mounts before Writer** | swap order → no crash | | Reader's `$derived` is actually **rendered** (live subscription) | declared-but-unrendered → no crash | | Writer writes the `$state` **during init** | — | | Page `{#await}` pending branch holds a **reactive root** (`{#each}`/`$derived`) | plain markup → no crash | | `ssr = false` | SSR default → no crash | ## Ruled out (red herrings from my first report) - **SvelteKit remote functions** — not required; any `{#await somePromise}` reproduces it. The handler body / return value / latency are irrelevant. - **bits-ui `Collapsible` + shadcn `Sidebar.Provider`** — reduce to the plain module-`$state` cross-write. No `Presence`, effects, `requestAnimationFrame`, `getBoundingClientRect`, Svelte attachments, context, or classes are needed.
title: experimental.async: "Batch has scheduled roots" when a sibling mutates shared $state during a suspense-resolution flush

### Describe the bug

Setting a new value for a key that already exists in a `SvelteMap` re-runs effects that only read the key set (`keys()`, `has()` misses), as long as that key was never read individually. Such a key has no source yet, so `set()` takes the new-key branch and increments the version signal unconditionally even though the key set didn't change. In practice `{#each [...map.keys()] as key}` re-renders on every value write into the map.

Fix incoming.
